items.title: Shiba
items.text:
A versatile computational method for systematic identification of differential RNA splicing. Shiba/scShiba can quantify and identify differential splicing events from bulk RNA-seq data and single-cell RNA-seq data. Shiba and scShiba are also implemented as Snakemake workflows, SnakeShiba and SnakeScShiba, respectively.

See CHANGELOG.md for the latest updates.

Report a bug

If you continue to encounter issues, please don't hesitate to open an issue on GitHub. The community and developers are here to help!

items.title: Bioconda package
items.text:
With the conda-forge and bioconda channels configured:

conda install shiba
shiba.py --help
scshiba.py --help

Run these commands in the activated environment where Shiba is installed. shiba.py and scshiba.py are on PATH; neither a source checkout nor a python ./ prefix is needed. For splicing-only analysis, use shiba.py --mame -p 4 config.yaml. The separate mameshiba package also provides shiba.py; there is no mameshiba command.

This guide describes the v1.0.0 implementation. Check the version printed by shiba.py --help. If Bioconda still supplies v0.8.2, use the matching source checkout for the new features. Installing new dependencies alone does not upgrade Shiba's code. Missing dependencies can be added with:

conda install -c conda-forge -c bioconda tosa=1.0.0 \
  r-glmmtmb=1.1.13 r-tmb=1.9.19 r-jsonlite=2.0 openpyxl=3.1

items.title: Locating scripts and workflows
items.text:
Only the two pipeline launchers are installed on PATH. For examples below that use internal scripts, bundled templates, or Snakefiles, set SHIBA_HOME to the directory containing the installed code:

SHIBA_HOME="$(python -c 'import pathlib, shutil; print(pathlib.Path(shutil.which("shiba.py")).resolve().parent)')"

For a source checkout, set SHIBA_HOME=/absolute/path/to/Shiba instead. Run its launchers as python "$SHIBA_HOME/shiba.py" or python "$SHIBA_HOME/scshiba.py" in place of shiba.py or scshiba.py in this guide. Creating an environment from environment.yml installs dependencies, but does not install these launchers on PATH.

For example, internal tools are invoked with python "$SHIBA_HOME/src/psi.py" --help, and workflows with snakemake -s "$SHIBA_HOME/snakeshiba.smk" --configfile config.yaml --cores 4. Use absolute paths in config and input tables to avoid depending on the directory from which you launch the command.

items.title: Dependencies for each analysis
items.text:
The new event-centric factorial regression uses R/glmmTMB for model fitting and jsonlite to exchange settings with Python. The table below distinguishes this requirement from the existing analysis modes.

Analysis Additional requirements Fisher splicing analysis (optional Welch t-test) Existing Python dependencies; glmmTMB/jsonlite are not required stat_method: beta_binomial R with glmmTMB and jsonlite Gene-expression differential analysis Existing R/DESeq2 dependencies, independently of the splicing mode Excel output openpyxl for all workbooks

The source checkout must contain src/beta_binomial_glm.R and the new --stat-method option in src/psi.py. Adding R packages does not update an older Shiba executable. The v0.8.2 package and image contain the earlier counting pipeline and do not include the factorial regression backend.

items.title: Source checkout
items.text:
Use the checkout containing the implementation you intend to run. If you are already working in that checkout, do not clone another copy. Otherwise, clone the repository and select the branch or release containing the new backend:

git clone https://github.com/Sika-Zheng-Lab/Shiba.git
cd Shiba
git switch develop # for a released build, select its release tag instead

Before continuing, confirm that the selected revision contains the backend:

test -f src/beta_binomial_glm.R

The source-installation commands below are run from this checkout. This explicitly selects the new source rather than the shiba.py executable installed by a previous Conda package. The new mode is configured as described in the beta-binomial regression guide.

items.title: Conda environment for a source checkout
New Shiba environment
items.text:
Use the checked-in environment shared by the source install, both Dockerfiles, and release validation. It includes Excel output and Snakemake:

conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate shiba
export PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1
python scripts/verify_runtime.py

The regression packages are available as r-glmmtmb and r-jsonlite on conda-forge. Installing them together lets Conda resolve their R and compiled-library dependencies. Python 3.12 was used for the regression integration tests; this is a tested configuration, not a claim that other Python versions cannot work.

Tosa 1.0.0 is used by this checkout for junction and intron-retention boundary counting in the bulk and single-cell pipelines. The commands above install it from Bioconda, making it available on PATH when the Conda environment is active. Tosa is not needed when running src/psi.py directly on existing compatible junction counts and event files.

For optional Excel output:

python -m pip install openpyxl

Run the checked-out pipeline after preparing config.yaml:

python ./shiba.py -p 4 config.yaml

items.title: Existing Shiba environment
items.text:
For reproducible release validation, create a separate environment from this checkout rather than updating an environment used for older analyses:

conda env create -n shiba-candidate -f environment.yml
conda activate shiba-candidate
python scripts/verify_runtime.py

Keep the environment used for older results available. Adding R packages alone does not replace an older Shiba executable; run the checked-out scripts.

items.title: MameShiba
items.text:
Use the same source environment and select splicing-only execution:

python ./shiba.py --mame -p 4 config.yaml

The regression backend is required when stat_method: beta_binomial is selected. --mame skips expression, PCA, plotting, and Excel output. The separately packaged MameShiba dependency set omits the expression backend; the v0.8.2 package does not supply the new factorial backend.

items.title: Installing the R backend with CRAN
items.text:
If you use a system or module-provided R rather than Conda, install both packages with the same Rscript executable that Shiba will use:

Rscript --vanilla -e 'install.packages(c("glmmTMB", "jsonlite"), repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")'

For a writable, version-specific user library, you can instead use:

export R_LIBS_USER="$HOME/.local/share/shiba/R-$(Rscript --vanilla -e 'cat(paste(R.version$major, strsplit(R.version$minor, ".", fixed=TRUE)[[1]][1], sep="."))')"
mkdir -p "$R_LIBS_USER"
Rscript --vanilla -e 'install.packages(c("glmmTMB", "jsonlite"), lib=Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_USER"), repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")'

Keep R_LIBS_USER set when running Shiba. A source installation may compile large C++ dependencies and requires appropriate build tools. Keep glmmTMB and its TMB/Matrix dependencies compatible; see the official glmmTMB installation guide for compilation requirements and binary-version mismatch troubleshooting.

By default, Shiba calls Rscript from PATH. To select another installation, use --rscript /path/to/Rscript with src/psi.py, or set this in the pipeline configuration:

rscript: /path/to/Rscript

The backend uses Rscript --vanilla, so it does not read .Rprofile. Install packages in a library visible to that executable through its standard library paths or R_LIBS_USER, rather than relying on .Rprofile to modify .libPaths(). Patsy and Formulaic are not used by the new statistical engine.

items.title: Verify the installation
items.text:
For the source checkout, run these checks from its root directory in the environment you will use for analysis. Package users can run shiba.py --help and python "$SHIBA_HOME/src/psi.py" --help using the location above. If you configured a custom rscript path, use that executable in the R checks too.

command -v python
command -v Rscript
python ./shiba.py --help
python ./src/psi.py --help
Rscript --vanilla -e 'stopifnot(requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly=TRUE), requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly=TRUE)); cat(R.version.string, "\n"); print(packageVersion("glmmTMB")); print(packageVersion("jsonlite"))'

src/psi.py --help should list --stat-method, --formula, --coef, and --contrast-file. For BAM/CRAM counting, also check:

tosa --version

From the source checkout (tests are not included in the release package), run a fitting check that uses bundled simulated data rather than your BAM files:

python -m unittest test.test_factorial.TestGlmmTMB.test_known_interaction_and_consistency -v

The test must report ok, not skipped; a skipped test means the R backend was not available to the test process. Full integration testing used R 4.5.2 with glmmTMB 1.1.13; selected numerical, event-type and prediction tests also passed with glmmTMB 1.1.15.2. These are tested versions, not hard minimum versions. Each analysis records its actual R/glmmTMB versions in design.json.

items.title: Docker
items.text:
Build from the source checkout so that the image contains the new scripts:

docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t shiba:factorial .
docker run --rm shiba:factorial tosa --version
docker run --rm shiba:factorial Rscript --vanilla -e 'stopifnot(requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly=TRUE), requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly=TRUE))'
docker run --rm shiba:factorial python /opt/Shiba/src/psi.py --help

Both docker/Dockerfile and docker/Dockerfile_develop install environment.yml with micromamba and copy the checked-out source into /opt/Shiba. The release image targets linux/amd64. CI records exact Conda packages, pip packages, R versions, and the source SHA, then runs every test with no skips. Optional shiba2sashimi is installed separately when needed; it is not required by these pipelines. shiba:factorial above is a local tag, not a published Docker Hub image.

Mount your working directory and start a shell:

docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work shiba:factorial bash

Inside the container, run shiba.py -p 4 config.yaml. Input, metadata, contrast, and output paths in the configuration must be accessible inside the container. The R packages must be installed in the image; installing them only on the host does not make them available inside a container.

Memory allocation

Large datasets may require a higher memory limit in Docker Desktop under Settings → Resources. Apply the new limit before restarting the container.

items.title: Snakemake
items.text:
Install Snakemake in the environment used to launch the workflow:

conda install -c conda-forge -c bioconda snakemake

Set SHIBA_HOME to the installed code or source checkout. To run with the activated Conda environment and its dependencies, omit container execution flags:

snakemake -s "$SHIBA_HOME/snakeshiba.smk" --configfile config.yaml --cores 4

For container execution, install Apptainer on the host and use an image built from the matching source checkout. For example, convert the Docker image built above into a local SIF image:

docker save shiba:factorial -o shiba-factorial.tar
apptainer build shiba-factorial.sif docker-archive:shiba-factorial.tar

Apptainer supports building SIF images from Docker archives; see its container build guide. Set the absolute path to the resulting SIF file in config.yaml:

container: /absolute/path/to/shiba-factorial.sif

Then run:

snakemake -s "$SHIBA_HOME/snakeshiba.smk" --configfile config.yaml --cores 4 --use-apptainer

--use-singularity is also supported as an alias in the Snakemake CLI. Ensure that the source checkout and all configured inputs/outputs are mounted inside the container; use --apptainer-args to add site-specific bind mounts. A locally built Docker tag is not automatically available as a docker:// registry image. Replace the example configuration's container URI with your local SIF or a registry image that contains the new backend.

These runtime setup steps also apply to SnakeScShiba, but the new factorial regression mode currently targets bulk biological replicate counts in SnakeShiba.

items.title: Fonts for publication figures
items.text: Arial is preferred for figures. If it is unavailable, static exports use Matplotlib's default DejaVu Sans; HTML uses Arial, sans-serif and the browser's fallback font. Optional SHIBA_FONT_DIR can point to a directory containing licensed Arial font files. Fonts are not bundled with this repository.

items.title: Output files of scShiba/SnakeScShiba
items.text:
All paths are relative to the configured workdir. Single-cell mode uses Fisher testing on counts aggregated by cell group; factorial beta-binomial regression is available only in the bulk workflow.

Path Contents events/EVENT_<TYPE>.txt Annotated event definitions for SE, FIVE, THREE, MXE, RI, MSE, AFE, and ALE. junctions/junctions.bed Tosa junction and RI-boundary counts aggregated by group. results/PSI_<TYPE>.txt Event annotations, observed group PSI, and differential results. In PSI-only mode, contains observed PSI without tests. results/summary.txt Differential-event counts by event type, annotation, and direction; differential runs only. results/PSI_matrix_sample.txt PSI matrix written only with only_psi: True; columns represent the groups in the aggregated count table despite the historical filename. results/results.xlsx Optional Excel export. plots/summary.html Self-contained interactive report with command provenance, summary counts, and volcano/PSI scatter plots for all eight types. PSI-only runs instead show labeled table previews. plots/png/, plots/pdf/, plots/svg/ Static figure exports for differential runs. plots/interactive/ Plot fragments embedded in the main HTML. plots/data/ Standalone event scatter and volcano HTML pages. report.json Pipeline command, version, input experiment table, and execution timing. benchmark/, log/ Rule resource measurements and logs added by SnakeScShiba.

Results are saved directly in results/, not results/splicing/. There are no expression or PCA outputs. Intermediate Tosa files may be removed by workflow cleanup.

See the Fisher column reference, single-cell quick start, and report regeneration instructions.

items.title: Output files of Shiba/SnakeShiba
items.text:
This page describes Fisher-mode result columns. For stat_method: beta_binomial, use the complete regression output reference; the two modes have different result schemas.

The output directory of Shiba contains the following sub directories:

  • annotation: Assembled GTF file, only when unannotated-event discovery is enabled.
  • events: Text files of alternative splicing events.
  • junctions: Junction read counts.
  • results: Results of differential expression and splicing analysis.
  • plots: Interactive summary.html, individual figure HTMLs, and PNG/PDF/SVG exports.
  • report.json: Pipeline command, version, inputs, and execution timing.

The following sub directories are added when SnakeShiba is used:

  • benchmark: Benchmarking results.
  • log: Log files of each step.

items.title: Files in results/splicing
items.text:
• PSI_[SE,FIVE,THREE,MXE,RI,MSE,AFE,ALE].txt: Results of differential splicing analysis.
  • PSI_matrix_[sample,group].txt: PSI values of each event for all samples or groups. Blank cells indicate that the event did not pass the minimum read count threshold.
  • analysis.json: Method and analysis settings.
  • results.xlsx: Optional Excel export.
  • summary.txt: Numbers of the differentially spliced events for each splicing and event type.

items.title: Column description of PSI_*.txt
items.text:
• event_id: ID of the event.
  • pos_id: Positional ID of the event. This is useful for comparing the same event across different Shiba runs.
  • strand: Strand of the event (+ or -).
  • gene_id: Gene ID.
  • gene_name: Gene name.
  • label: Label of the event type (annotated or unannotated). annotated means that the event is documented in the reference annotation file, while unannotated means that the event is NOT documented in the reference annotation file (i.e. novel or cryptic splicing event).
  • ref_PSI: PSI of the reference group.
  • alt_PSI: PSI of the alternative group.
  • dPSI: Delta PSI (alt_PSI - ref_PSI).
  • q: P-value of Fisher's exact test adjusted by the Benjamini-Hochberg method.
  • Diff events: Flag of if the event is differentially spliced between the reference and alternative groups (Yes or No).

items.title: PSI_SE.txt
items.text:
Skipped exon
  • exon: Genomic coordinates of the skipped exon.
  • intron_a: Genomic coordinates of the left-side inclusive intron of the skipped exon.
  • intron_b: Genomic coordinates of the right-side inclusive intron of the skipped exon.
  • intron_c: Genomic coordinates of the exclusive intron of the skipped exon.
  • ref_junction_a: Junction read counts of the left-side inclusive intron of the skipped exon in the reference group.
  • ref_junction_b: Junction read counts of the right-side inclusive intron of the skipped exon in the reference group.
  • ref_junction_c: Junction read counts of the exclusive intron of the skipped exon in the reference group.
  • alt_junction_a: Junction read counts of the left-side inclusive intron of the skipped exon in the alternative group.
  • alt_junction_b: Junction read counts of the right-side inclusive intron of the skipped exon in the alternative group.
  • alt_junction_c: Junction read counts of the exclusive intron of the skipped exon in the alternative group.
  • OR_junction_a: Odds ratio comparing junction read counts of the left-side inclusive intron to those of the exclusive intron, reference group against alternative group.
  • p_junction_a: P-value of Fisher's exact test for the junction read counts of the left-side inclusive intron to those of the exclusive intron, reference group against alternative group.
  • OR_junction_b: Odds ratio comparing junction read counts of the right-side inclusive intron to those of the exclusive intron, reference group against alternative group.
  • p_junction_b: P-value of Fisher's exact test for the junction read counts of the right-side inclusive intron to those of the exclusive intron, reference group against alternative group.
  • p_maximum: Greater of the two P-values of Fisher's exact tests.

items.title: PSI_FIVE.txt and PSI_THREE.txt
items.text:
Alternative 5' and 3' splice sites
  • exon_a: Genomic coordinates of the longer exon using more internal splice site.
  • exon_b: Genomic coordinates of the shorter exon using less internal splice site.
  • intron_a: Genomic coordinates of the intron associated with the longer exon.
  • intron_b: Genomic coordinates of the intron associated with the shorter exon.
  • ref_junction_a: Junction read counts of the intron associated with the longer exon in the reference group.
  • ref_junction_b: Junction read counts of the intron associated with the shorter exon in the reference group.
  • alt_junction_a: Junction read counts of the intron associated with the longer exon in the alternative group.
  • alt_junction_b: Junction read counts of the intron associated with the shorter exon in the alternative group.
  • OR: Odds ratio comparing junction read counts of the intron associated with the longer exon to those of the intron associated with the shorter exon, reference group against alternative group.
  • p: P-value of Fisher's exact test for the junction read counts of the intron associated with the longer exon to those of the intron associated with the shorter exon, reference group against alternative group.

items.title: PSI_MXE.txt
items.text:
Mutually exclusive exons Exon A/B follow transcript orientation; on the minus strand, A is not the leftmost exon. Junctions a1/b1 are upstream (5′) and a2/b2 are downstream (3′) of their respective exon in transcript orientation.
  • exon_a: Genomic coordinates of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation).
  • exon_b: Genomic coordinates of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation).
  • intron_a1: Genomic coordinates of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation).
  • intron_a2: Genomic coordinates of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation).
  • intron_b1: Genomic coordinates of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation).
  • intron_b2: Genomic coordinates of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation).
  • ref_junction_a1: Junction read counts of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) in the reference group.
  • ref_junction_a2: Junction read counts of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) in the reference group.
  • ref_junction_b1: Junction read counts of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) in the reference group.
  • ref_junction_b2: Junction read counts of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) in the reference group.
  • alt_junction_a1: Junction read counts of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) in the alternative group.
  • alt_junction_a2: Junction read counts of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) in the alternative group.
  • alt_junction_b1: Junction read counts of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) in the alternative group.
  • alt_junction_b2: Junction read counts of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) in the alternative group.
  • OR_junction_a1b1: Odds ratio comparing junction read counts of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) to those of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation), reference group against alternative group.
  • p_junction_a1b1: P-value of Fisher's exact test for the junction read counts of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) to those of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation), reference group against alternative group.
  • OR_junction_a1b2: Odds ratio comparing junction read counts of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) to those of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation), reference group against alternative group.
  • p_junction_a1b2: P-value of Fisher's exact test comparing junction read counts of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) to those of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation), reference group against alternative group.
  • OR_junction_a2b1: Odds ratio comparing junction read counts of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) to those of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation), reference group against alternative group.
  • p_junction_a2b1: P-value of Fisher's exact test comparing junction read counts of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) to those of the upstream (5′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation), reference group against alternative group.
  • OR_junction_a2b2: Odds ratio comparing junction read counts of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) to those of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation), reference group against alternative group.
  • p_junction_a2b2: P-value of Fisher's exact test comparing junction read counts of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the upstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation) to those of the downstream (3′) inclusive intron of the downstream mutually exclusive exon (in transcript orientation), reference group against alternative group.
  • p_maximum: Greater of the four P-values of Fisher's exact tests.

items.title: PSI_RI.txt
items.text:
Retained intron
  • exon_a: Genomic coordinates of the left-side exon.
  • exon_b: Genomic coordinates of the right-side exon.
  • exon_c: Genomic coordinates of the exon containing the retained intron.
  • intron_a: Genomic coordinates of the retained intron.
  • ref_junction_a: Junction read counts of the intron in the reference group.
  • ref_junction_a_start: The left-side exon-intron junction read counts of the retained intron in the reference group.
  • ref_junction_a_end: The right-side exon-intron junction read counts of the retained intron in the reference group.
  • alt_junction_a: Junction read counts of the intron in the alternative group.
  • alt_junction_a_start: The left-side exon-intron junction read counts of the retained intron in the alternative group.
  • alt_junction_a_end: The right-side exon-intron junction read counts of the retained intron in the alternative group.
  • OR_junction_a_start: Odds ratio comparing the left-side exon-intron junction read counts to the intron junction read counts, reference group against alternative group.
  • p_junction_a_start: P-value of Fisher's exact test for the left-side exon-intron junction read counts to the intron junction read counts, reference group against alternative group.
  • OR_junction_a_end: Odds ratio comparing the right-side exon-intron junction read counts to the intron junction read counts, reference group against alternative group.
  • p_junction_a_end: P-value of Fisher's exact test for the right-side exon-intron junction read counts to the intron junction read counts, reference group against alternative group.
  • p_maximum: Greater of the two P-values of Fisher's exact tests.

items.title: PSI_MSE.txt
items.text:
Multiple skipped exons
  • mse_n: Number of skipped exons.
  • exon: Genomic coordinates of the skipped exons, separated by semi-colons from the left to the right (e.g., chr1:75790152-75790274;chr1:75790446-75790517).
  • intron: Genomic coordinates of the associated introns of the skipped exons, separated by semi-colons from the left to the right and the last one is the exclusive intron (e.g., chr1:75790057-75790152;chr1:75790274-75790446;chr1:75790517-75791285;chr1:75790057-75791285).
  • ref_junction: Junction read counts of the associated introns of the skipped exons in the reference group, separated by semi-colons from the left to the right and the last one is the exclusive intron (e.g., 25;20;32;489).
  • alt_junction: Junction read counts of the associated introns of the skipped exons in the alternative group, separated by semi-colons from the left to the right and the last one is the exclusive intron (e.g., 386;438;703;598).
  • OR_junction: Odds ratio comparing junction read counts of the associated inclusive introns of the skipped exons to those of the exclusive intron, reference group against alternative group, separated by semi-colons from the left to the right (e.g., 0.07920361952594382;0.05584036006760605;0.055665610718888085).
  • p_junction: P-value of Fisher's exact test for the junction read counts of the associated inclusive introns of the skipped exons to those of the exclusive intron, reference group against alternative group, separated by semi-colons from the left to the right (e.g., 3.0283773991245187e-54;2.488569122823104e-66;3.7054604961481054e-93).

items.title: PSI_AFE.txt and PSI_ALE.txt
items.text:
Alternative first and last exons
  • exon_a: Genomic coordinates of the distal exons, separated by semi-colons from the distal to the proximal (e.g., chr11:30267948-30268175;chr11:30219579-30219772).
  • exon_b: Genomic coordinates of the proximal exons, separated by semi-colons from the distal to the proximal (e.g., chr11:30197724-30198257).
  • intron_a: Genomic coordinates of the introns associated with the distal exon, separated by semi-colons from the distal to the proximal (e.g., chr11:30219772-30267948;chr11:30159445-30219579).
  • intron_b: Genomic coordinates of the introns associated with the proximal exon, separated by semi-colons from the distal to the proximal (e.g., chr11:30159445-30197724).
  • ref_junction_a: Junction read counts of the introns associated with the distal exon in the reference group, separated by semi-colons from the distal to the proximal (e.g., 184;451).
  • ref_junction_b: Junction read counts of the introns associated with the proximal exon in the reference group, separated by semi-colons from the distal to the proximal (e.g., 136).
  • alt_junction_a: Junction read counts of the introns associated with the distal exon in the alternative group, separated by semi-colons from the distal to the proximal (e.g., 975;3058).
  • alt_junction_b: Junction read counts of the introns associated with the proximal exon in the alternative group, separated by semi-colons from the distal to the proximal (e.g., 4).
  • OR_junction: Odds ratio comparing junction read counts of the introns associated with the distal exon to those of the introns associated with the proximal exon, reference group against alternative group, separated by semi-colons from the distal to the proximal. (e.g., 0.00555052790346908;0.0043377063055438005).
  • p_junction: P-value of Fisher's exact test for the junction read counts of the introns associated with the distal exon to those of the introns associated with the proximal exon, reference group against alternative group, separated by semi-colons from the distal to the proximal (e.g., 3.952031792878382e-88;5.615960667265659e-108).

items.title: when ttest is true
items.text:
• <sample>_PSI: PSI of the sample. Blank cells indicate that the event did not pass the minimum read count threshold.
  • p_ttest: P-value of Welch's t-test for the PSI of the reference and alternative groups. Please note that the P-value is not adjusted for multiple testing.

items.title: Factorial beta-binomial analysis
items.text:
Use the dedicated config with these matching templates:

File Purpose samples.tsv Sample metadata for genotype * treatment + batch Shiba_experiment.tsv Matching sample IDs, BAM paths, and pipeline group labels contrasts.json Optional interaction and drug effects within WT and KO predictions.json Optional fitted PSI profiles and drug/interaction PSI effects

These are input templates, not a runnable sequencing dataset. They contain 16 illustrative biological replicates: WT/KO × Control/Drug × B1/B2, with two replicates per cell. Replace the rows with your independent biological samples; do not duplicate samples to fill the design. BAM files and a matching reference GTF must be supplied separately. Install the dependencies in the installation guide, including R/glmmTMB and jsonlite.

Set SHIBA_HOME to the installed package or source directory, then prepare a directory (choose a new directory to avoid overwriting existing configuration files):

mkdir -p factorial_example
cp "$SHIBA_HOME/example/Shiba_SnakeShiba_beta_binomial_config_example.yaml" factorial_example/config.yaml
cp "$SHIBA_HOME/example/beta_binomial/samples.tsv" factorial_example/samples.tsv
cp "$SHIBA_HOME/example/beta_binomial/Shiba_experiment.tsv" factorial_example/Shiba_experiment.tsv
cp "$SHIBA_HOME/example/beta_binomial/contrasts.json" factorial_example/contrasts.json
cp "$SHIBA_HOME/example/beta_binomial/predictions.json" factorial_example/predictions.json

Before running, edit the copied files:

  1. Set absolute workdir (output directory), gtf, experiment_table, and sample_metadata paths in config.yaml, and actual BAM paths in Shiba_experiment.tsv. Use the same unique sample IDs in both TSV files.
  2. Adjust formula, categorical, reference_levels, and coef to your experimental design. The supplied config tests genotypeKO:treatmentDrug. group labels are used by the pipeline; regression uses the metadata factors.
  3. Keep stat_method: beta_binomial. stat_method: fisher, or omitting it, selects Fisher testing. The removed top-level beta_binomial: true/false switch must not be used.

With the Conda environment activated, run the complete pipeline, including expression abundance, PCA, and reports. For a source checkout, substitute python "$SHIBA_HOME/shiba.py" for shiba.py:

shiba.py factorial_example/config.yaml -p 8

For splicing only, or to reuse existing events and junction counts under the configured workdir, respectively:

shiba.py factorial_example/config.yaml -p 8 --mame
shiba.py factorial_example/config.yaml -p 8 --start-step 4 --mame

To run all three example contrasts, comment out coef and set contrast_file to the absolute path of the copied contrasts.json. Set prediction_grid to the copied predictions.json for the corresponding PSI profiles/effects. The interaction tests a difference of effects on the log-odds scale; delta_delta is a PSI-scale difference of differences and is not the same numerical effect. Batch is averaged over the observed samples in these prediction profiles.

Coverage filtering defaults to at least 10 reads in the same half of samples in every categorical design cell, including batch. In the example, each of the eight cells has two samples, so at least one sample per cell must meet coverage for all components. To explicitly group coverage by genotype × treatment only, uncomment filter_group: [genotype, treatment]; each of those four groups then has four samples, requiring at least two. This changes the filter, not the model.

Results are written under <workdir>/results/splicing/, including event_statistics.tsv, event_filter.tsv, design.json, and, when requested, model_predictions.tsv. See the regression guide for contrast definitions and interpretation. Gene-expression differential testing is a separate pairwise analysis enabled by expression_reference_group and expression_alternative_group; the splicing formula is not applied to expression.

items.title: Differential RNA splicing analysis with bulk RNA-seq data
Before you start
items.text:
This guide uses the default stat_method: fisher. For factorial regression, use the beta-binomial quick start.

  • Perform mapping of RNA-seq reads to the reference genome and generate bam files with their index files (.bai) by software such as STAR and HISAT2.
    • You can download test RNA-seq bam files with their index (two replicates for reference and alternative groups) mapped by STAR on the mouse genome from here.
  • Download a gene annotation file of your interest in GTF format.

items.text: Follow the installation guide and activate the environment containing Shiba. The commands below use the Conda-installed launchers. For a source checkout, use the source invocation instead. These examples require the v1.0.0 implementation, including Tosa.

items.title: 1. Prepare inputs
items.text:
experiment.tsv: A tab-separated text file of sample ID, path to bam files, and groups for differential analysis.

sample  bam group
Ref_1 /path/to/workdir/bam/Ref_1.bam  Ref
Ref_2 /path/to/workdir/bam/Ref_2.bam  Ref
Alt_1 /path/to/workdir/bam/Alt_1.bam  Alt
Alt_2 /path/to/workdir/bam/Alt_2.bam  Alt

Make sure to use tabs

If you copy and paste the above example, your experiment.tsv file may contain spaces instead of tabs, which will causes an error when you run Shiba. Please make sure that you are using a tab character between the columns.

Shiba supports long-read RNA-seq data

If you have long-read RNA-seq data (i.e., PacBio or ONT), please add the 4th column to the experiment.tsv file with the value long for long-read data and short for short-read data. For example:

sample bam group technology
Ref_1 /path/to/workdir/bam/Ref_1.bam Ref short
Ref_2 /path/to/workdir/bam/Ref_2.bam Ref long
Alt_1 /path/to/workdir/bam/Alt_1.bam Alt short
Alt_2 /path/to/workdir/bam/Alt_2.bam Alt long

If you want to use long-read RNA-seq data only for discovery of alternative RNA splicing events and NOT for differential analysis, you can set the 3rd column to different values than that of short-read data. For example, if you want to perform differential splicing analysis between Ref and Alt groups using short-read data, you can set Ref and Alt for short-read data, and set Ref_long and Alt_long for long-read data, so that the long-read data will be used only for transcript assembly and not for differential analysis.

After installing Shiba, activate its Conda environment and prepare config.yaml. These examples use the installed launchers. For a source checkout, substitute the source invocation. Fisher analysis also uses -p N to distribute event tests across processes. BH correction is applied after joining results, across the same event-type family as before. Small workloads (fewer than 256 input events per type) run serially; larger workloads use up to N workers. Each process caches up to 10,000 identical 2×2 tables. This cache is separate from the factorial component_cache_size setting.

RI boundary counting defaults to boundary_anchor_length: 6 (six aligned bases on each side). Explicit config values override this default. When changing it, regenerate Tosa counts from the alignments with the same setting for counting and merging; do not reuse intermediate boundary tables made with another value.

items.title: Event-centric beta-binomial regression
items.text: Shiba and SnakeShiba support an optional stat_method: beta_binomial mode for factorial differential splicing. Python extracts integer junction comparisons; R/glmmTMB fits each component across biological replicates. The default fisher mode runs Fisher testing, with an optional Welch t-test. The old supplementary beta_binomial option and psi.py -b/--beta-binomial have been removed.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
Use Shiba v1.0.0 or the matching source checkout, with R packages glmmTMB and jsonlite installed in the R environment used by Rscript. For an existing Conda environment:

conda activate shiba
conda install -c conda-forge r-glmmtmb r-jsonlite
Rscript --vanilla -e 'stopifnot(requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly=TRUE), requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly=TRUE))'

See the installation guide for new Shiba/MameShiba environments, CRAN and user-library installation, verification, and Docker or SnakeShiba container setup. Installing the packages alone does not add this mode to an older Shiba executable. Set SHIBA_HOME before using the internal-script examples below. For a source checkout, replace shiba.py with python "$SHIBA_HOME/shiba.py".

--rscript /path/to/Rscript selects another R installation; the corresponding pipeline setting is rscript. The backend uses Rscript --vanilla, so a custom library must be visible through standard R library paths or R_LIBS_USER. Shiba records R and glmmTMB versions in design.json. No Patsy or Formulaic is used by the new engine.

Matching sample metadata, experiment table, contrasts, and prediction profiles are provided for the dedicated config. See the factorial quick start for copying, editing, and running them. These templates require your own BAMs and reference GTF.

items.title: Inputs and model
items.text:
Use the existing junctions.bed and EVENT_*.txt files. Supply metadata with one row per independent biological replicate and exactly the same sample IDs as the junction table. Row order does not matter. Missing covariates, duplicate sample IDs and rank-deficient designs are errors; samples are not silently discarded.

sample  genotype  treatment  batch
WT_C_1  WT        Control    B1
WT_C_2  WT        Control    B2
WT_D_1  WT        Drug       B1
WT_D_2  WT        Drug       B2
KO_C_1  KO        Control    B1
KO_C_2  KO        Control    B2
KO_D_1  KO        Drug       B1
KO_D_2  KO        Drug       B2

The actual file must be tab-separated. In full pipelines, keep the usual sample, bam, group experiment table and supply a separate metadata file. group remains a label for the existing pipeline, not a restriction to two regression groups. The standalone psi.py regression does not require group.

For component c of event e and sample s:

K_ecs ~ BetaBinomial(N_ecs, mu_ecs, rho_ec)
N_ecs = inclusion_ecs + exclusion_ecs
logit(mu_ecs) = X_s beta_ec

Dispersion is estimated separately for each event/component, constant across samples (dispformula = ~1). Reported phi is glmmTMB's concentration parameter; rho = 1 / (1 + phi) is the overdispersion parameter. There is no across-event shrinkage. This initial implementation accepts fixed-effect formulas only; random effects, offsets, smooths and arbitrary R function calls are rejected.

Supported formula algebra includes +, -, *, :, /, ^, parentheses, and intercept removal (~ 0 + condition). Examples:

~ genotype * treatment + batch
~ condition + sex + batch
~ genotype * time
~ genotype * treatment * sex

Numeric columns are continuous by default; other columns become factors. Use repeatable --categorical / --continuous options to override inference. Factor levels are sorted, and --reference-level FACTOR=LEVEL sets a baseline. Do not interpret numeric time as a categorical time course without declaring it.

items.title: CLI
items.text:
First inspect the actual R coefficient names:

python "$SHIBA_HOME/src/psi.py" junctions.bed events design_check \
  --stat-method beta_binomial --sample-metadata samples.tsv \
  --formula 'genotype * treatment + batch' \
  --reference-level genotype=WT --reference-level treatment=Control \
  --design-only

Then test the interaction:

python "$SHIBA_HOME/src/psi.py" junctions.bed events results \
  --stat-method beta_binomial --sample-metadata samples.tsv \
  --formula 'genotype * treatment + batch' \
  --reference-level genotype=WT --reference-level treatment=Control \
  --coef 'genotypeKO:treatmentDrug' -p 4

R coefficient names (for example genotypeKO:treatmentDrug) are used, rather than Patsy-style names. Repeat --coef to test several coefficients. Use a separate output directory for design inspection so that it does not replace the design metadata associated with an existing analysis.

Arbitrary scalar linear contrasts are supplied as a JSON file:

{
  "interaction": {"genotypeKO:treatmentDrug": 1},
  "drug_in_KO": {"treatmentDrug": 1, "genotypeKO:treatmentDrug": 1},
  "reversed_interaction": {"genotypeKO:treatmentDrug": -1}
}

Pass --contrast-file contrasts.json. Each contrast tests c' beta = 0 using a full versus constrained-null likelihood-ratio test with one degree of freedom. The null design uses a basis for the null space of c', so a general contrast is not approximated by removing a single formula term. Multi-degree-of-freedom omnibus tests are not part of this interface; factors with three or more levels are supported through their coefficients and scalar contrasts.

items.title: Component definitions and event calls
items.text:
Event Inclusion/exclusion comparisons SE a/c and b/c MSE every inclusion junction / the final skipping junction FIVE, THREE a/b MXE a1/b1, a1/b2, a2/b1, a2/b2 RI start boundary / spliced junction; end boundary / spliced junction AFE, ALE all A-side / B-side junction pairs

RI's positive direction means increased retention. MXE uses the current strand-aware exon A orientation. Absent junction IDs have zero counts. Negative, fractional, non-finite or inexactly representable input counts are rejected. No inclusion averages or duplicated skipping counts enter the likelihood.

For each event, a sample is eligible only if every required component has inclusion + exclusion >= --minimum-reads (default 10). All components use this same sample set. Before fitting, the event must have eligible samples in at least half of every group (--min-sample-fraction 0.5, the default). The required number is rounded up: two eligible samples in a group of three, for example. Counts are evaluated per component and sample, not pooled across samples or junctions.

By default, groups are the observed combinations of all categorical factors in the model formula, regardless of whether metadata has a group column. For genotype * treatment, these are genotype × treatment cells. A categorical batch in the formula also splits the cells; continuous covariates do not. Numeric-coded categories must be declared using --categorical (or reference levels) as usual. With no categorical factors, all samples form one group. Override the grouping columns explicitly when needed, for example:

--filter-group genotype --filter-group treatment --min-sample-fraction 0.5

Only coverage-passing events are sent to glmmTMB and included in FDR correction. Filtered events remain in event output with status = filtered_low_coverage, missing P/Q values and Diff events = No; event_filter.tsv records eligible and required sample counts per group. Observed PSI tables still contain all input events. Coverage screening does not use observed effect direction or P values. After screening, the remaining design must retain full rank and have more samples than mean coefficients plus one dispersion parameter. This is an identifiability check, not a guarantee of reliable small-sample inference.

An event requires all component fits and tests to succeed, and all tested contrast estimates to have the same nonzero sign. Its P value is the maximum component P value. Contradictory directions give p_event = 1. A missing, boundary-only or failed component gives an untestable event; other components cannot rescue it. Components sharing junctions are not assumed independent, and their likelihoods are not added together.

By default BH correction pools all eight event types, separately for each contrast. --p-adjust BY requests the more conservative arbitrary-dependence correction. Only events passing the coverage filter enter each correction family. If a passing event is subsequently untestable or fails fitting, it contributes P=1 internally but displays missing P/Q values. Separate contrast families do not provide FDR control over a subsequently selected union of all contrasts. Shared junctions between events can also induce dependence; BH's usual dependence assumptions apply.

Diff events uses event Q < --fdr and the consistency rule. Legacy odds-ratio and -d/--psi cutoffs do not apply. An optional biological relevance filter uses --effect-name NAME --min-effect VALUE after correction; the Q values still refer to logit-scale tests, not an effect-size-threshold null hypothesis.

items.title: PSI predictions and effect sizes
items.text:
For a single selected contrast involving one or two binary categorical factors, Shiba automatically generates their condition profiles. Other covariates retain the same empirical distribution in every profile: predictions are averaged equally over all design samples, not pooled by read depth. For two factors, the first varies between strata and the second defines within-stratum changes. The resulting PSI effects include the two changes and their difference.

For other designs, or multiple contrasts, explicitly provide --prediction-grid predictions.json:

{
  "profiles": {
    "WT_Control": {"genotype": "WT", "treatment": "Control"},
    "WT_Drug": {"genotype": "WT", "treatment": "Drug"},
    "KO_Control": {"genotype": "KO", "treatment": "Control"},
    "KO_Drug": {"genotype": "KO", "treatment": "Drug"}
  },
  "effects": {
    "delta_WT": {"WT_Drug": 1, "WT_Control": -1},
    "delta_KO": {"KO_Drug": 1, "KO_Control": -1},
    "delta_delta": {"KO_Drug": 1, "KO_Control": -1, "WT_Drug": -1, "WT_Control": 1}
  }
}

Numeric settings also support chosen time/dose values. Profile values must be valid for the design; users are responsible for avoiding extrapolation outside supported covariate combinations. PSI effect weights must sum to zero.

Component predictions are fitted inclusion probabilities. Event predictions and PSI effects are the equal-weight mean across all required components; they are not identical to historical Shiba PSI based on mean junction counts. Historical observed PSI is retained separately, including its existing coverage rule. The current implementation reports point predictions without PSI-scale confidence intervals. Coefficient intervals are approximate Wald intervals; P values come from the LRT.

A logit interaction of zero does not imply a PSI-scale difference-in-differences of zero. The regression P value must not be presented as testing delta-delta PSI. Likewise, component direction consistency is enforced on the tested logit contrast; it does not assert equality of component effect magnitudes.

items.title: Locations and execution modes
items.text:
For shiba.py config.yaml and SnakeShiba, all paths below are relative to the configured workdir:

workdir/
├── annotation/                  # Optional transcript assembly
├── events/                      # EVENT_<TYPE>.txt definitions
├── junctions/                   # junctions.bed and counting intermediates
├── results/
│   ├── splicing/                # All regression files listed below
│   ├── expression/              # Counts, abundance, optional DESeq2 results
│   └── pca/                     # TPM and observed-PSI PCA
├── plots/
│   ├── summary.html             # Main self-contained interactive report
│   ├── figure_style.json
│   ├── png/
│   ├── pdf/
│   ├── svg/
│   ├── interactive/             # Embedded plot fragments
│   └── data/                    # Standalone PCA HTMLs, when PCA is included
└── report.json                  # Pipeline execution provenance

<TYPE> is one of SE, FIVE, THREE, MXE, RI, MSE, AFE, or ALE. A standalone src/psi.py run writes the regression files directly into its output argument, without creating expression, PCA, or HTML reports. To use the reporting command below, choose results/splicing as that output and pass its parent results to plots.py.

shiba.py --mame stops after splicing and does not generate expression, PCA, or plots. A successful standalone --design-only run produces only design_matrix.tsv, contrasts.tsv, design.json, and glmmTMB.log; it does not fit events or generate the remaining regression outputs.

items.title: Regression files in results/splicing/
items.text:
All files in this table are written by a successful full regression run, except the explicitly optional Excel workbook. Some tables can contain headers only when there are no applicable results.

File Contents and use event_statistics.tsv Main results across all event types: one row per event/contrast, event annotations, p_event, q_event, status, component effect summaries, and Diff events. Start here for downstream analysis; select the intended contrast before comparing events. PSI_<TYPE>.txt The same event/contrast results split by event type. Despite the historical filename, these are regression results, not the legacy two-group Fisher schema. Sample *_PSI columns are added when --individual-psi is enabled. component_statistics.tsv One row per tested component/contrast: logit estimate, Wald se/ci_low/ci_high, LRT lr and p_component, dispersion phi/rho, full/null log likelihoods, eligible sample count, convergence/Hessian flags, status, and diagnostic. Coverage-filtered events are not fitted. components.tsv Definitions for all input events, including filtered events: component IDs and inclusion/exclusion junction IDs. Use to link a component result back to its junction comparison. event_filter.tsv One row per event/filter group: n_samples, n_eligible, n_required, group_pass, and overall filter_pass. filter_group identifies the categorical cell. Use this table to explain coverage exclusions. component_predictions.tsv Component-level predictions: kind distinguishes profiles from effects, name identifies the profile/effect, and value contains fitted PSI or a PSI-scale contrast. Header-only when no predictions are available. model_predictions.tsv Event-level equal-weight component means for each kind/name, with component_min, component_max, and status. Incomplete component sets have missing numeric values and incomplete_components status; the file itself is still created. Ranges are not confidence intervals. observed_PSI_<TYPE>.tsv Historical observed PSI and junction-count columns, separately from model predictions. Includes input events regardless of the regression coverage filter. PSI_matrix_sample.txt Observed event-by-sample PSI matrix used for PCA; not fitted PSI. This mode does not generate PSI_matrix_group.txt. design_matrix.tsv Actual numeric R model matrix, with sample IDs and one column per coefficient. contrasts.tsv One row per coefficient and one column per named contrast, giving its weights. design.json Formula, coefficient names, factor levels, prediction definitions, target hypothesis/population, and R/glmmTMB versions. sample_metadata.tsv Metadata used by the analysis, aligned to the analysis samples. Factor coding and reference levels should be checked in design.json and design_matrix.tsv. analysis.json Analysis manifest: method/backend, formula, contrasts, FDR method/family/threshold, coverage settings and groups, event/sample counts, effect-filter settings, process count, batch limit, and cache size. Also identifies the regression report mode. glmmTMB.log R backend output from design construction and fitting; inspect alongside component diagnostics if a run or fit fails. summary.txt Counts (Number) grouped by event_type, contrast, status, and Diff events. Counts across contrasts can include the same event more than once. factorial_results.xlsx Optional (--excel / excel: True): eight event-type sheets plus model_predictions. It does not replace the component, filter, or diagnostic TSV files. stage_timings.tsv Python orchestration stages and elapsed wall-clock seconds for each stage. component_timings.tsv Per-component elapsed/full/null fitting time, optimizer attempts, retries, worker PID, and cache-hit information. batch_timings.tsv Per-batch component/fitted-component counts, cache hits, optimizer attempts, retries, and elapsed seconds. backend_performance.json Backend process/scheduling/cache settings and aggregate workload, cache, optimizer, retry, and elapsed-time measurements.

Timing files describe different levels of the same computation; do not add worker times to batch or stage times to estimate total wall time. When no events pass coverage, fitting/prediction tables and per-component/per-batch timings are empty, while filter results and backend totals still document the outcome. Internal .factorial-*/ batch TSVs, configuration JSON, and design.rds are temporary working files, not retained analysis products.

items.title: Figures and HTML in plots/
items.text:
File or pattern Contents and generation condition summary.html Self-contained interactive report: command provenance, analysis settings, discovery counts, contrast/status summaries, available PSI effects/PCA, and previews of the first 200 event/prediction rows. Full tables remain in the TSV files. figure_style.json Resolved static font paths, export DPI, and export formats. png/<name>.png Static 300-dpi figure exports. pdf/<name>.pdf, svg/<name>.svg Static publication exports; dense scatter points can be rasterized. interactive/<name>.html Plot fragments assembled into the main HTML. These are not standalone pages and do not need to accompany summary.html. data/pca_TPM.html, data/pca_PSI.html Standalone interactive PCA pages, created only when the corresponding PCA data and experiment table are supplied.

The figure <name> values are:

  • barplot_splicing_summary: significant-event counts per contrast, stacked by event type.
  • contrast_1, contrast_2, …: conservative logit component effect versus −log10(event Q), one figure for each contrast present in the event table. Numbering follows contrast appearance in that table; the HTML heading/caption gives the contrast name.
  • psi_effect_1, psi_effect_2, …: at most 20 events with the largest absolute finite model PSI effect for each available effect name. Numbering follows effect-name appearance; figures are omitted when there are no finite effects.
  • pca_TPM and pca_PSI: optional sample PCA figures, requiring their PCA tables and an experiment table.

items.title: Other full-pipeline outputs
items.text:
These files are shared with the bulk workflow; their availability depends on the selected steps and configuration.

Path relative to workdir Contents annotation/assembled_annotation.gtf Assembled annotation when unannotated-event discovery is enabled, with assembly intermediates in the same directory. events/EVENT_<TYPE>.txt Event definitions used for counting and splicing analysis. junctions/junctions.bed Combined sample count table used by the regression. Counting intermediates vary with workflow and cleanup settings. results/expression/counts.txt Gene count matrix. results/expression/TPM.txt, results/expression/CPM.txt Gene abundance matrices; TPM supplies expression PCA. results/expression/DEG.txt Pairwise DESeq2 results only when both expression comparison groups are supplied. This is not factorial splicing output. results/expression/TPM_CPM.xlsx Optional expression workbook when Excel export is enabled. results/pca/tpm_pca.tsv, results/pca/psi_pca.tsv Sample principal-component scores for TPM and observed PSI. results/pca/tpm_contribution.tsv, results/pca/psi_contribution.tsv Explained variance fractions for each principal component. report.json Pipeline execution provenance, including command, version, input experiment table, and timing. Not generated by standalone psi.py. log/, benchmark/ SnakeShiba rule logs and resource/timing records. These directories are not automatically created by the Python launcher.

items.title: Reading results and reports
items.text:
An event has no single fitted regression coefficient: estimate_min/max and conservative_component_effect summarize component coefficients, while the actual estimates remain in the component table. conservative_component_effect is the signed estimate with smallest absolute magnitude, used for the regression report's horizontal axis. Legacy output columns are unchanged in legacy mode; consumers of the new mode must use its explicit schema.

The full pipeline's report recognizes analysis.json and displays contrasts without assuming a single reference/alternative PSI pair. It writes the existing plots/summary.html and summary plot paths. The standalone regression report can also be generated with src/plots.py using a parent results directory containing splicing/.

Both Fisher and beta-binomial reports use the same interactive Plotly theme: white backgrounds, thin axes, restrained colors, and compact typography. HTML uses larger screen-readable labels and markers than the static publication exports. The analysis command passed by the pipeline is shown at the top; when regenerating reports, --shiba-command overrides the command recorded in the parent report.json. Missing provenance is explicitly marked as not recorded. Hover to inspect samples/events, zoom or pan, and click legend entries to show/hide traces. Plotly JavaScript and figure data are embedded in one summary.html, so no network connection is required. Figures are rendered as they enter the viewport to bound WebGL resource use; axis/legend state is retained when scrolling. Static PNG (300 dpi), PDF, and SVG exports remain in png/, pdf/, and svg/. Browser toolbar export saves the current view as SVG (WebGL scatter points may be rasterized).

Arial is preferred; when unavailable, static exports use DejaVu Sans and the browser uses its default sans-serif font. SHIBA_FONT_DIR optionally supplies local font files. figure_style.json records font paths for regression exports.

Each contrast has a significance/effect scatter and status counts. Optional model PSI effects display at most 20 events with the largest absolute effect, without a significance filter; this selection is stated in the caption. No additional tests or confidence intervals are inferred. Missing coordinates are omitted with counts reported, and zero q-values are clipped only for log display. When PCA files and an experiment table are available, sample PCA figures are included. Embedded result tables show the first 200 rows; complete TSVs remain in the analysis output directory.

python "$SHIBA_HOME/src/plots.py" -i /path/to/results -o /path/to/plots \
  -e /path/to/Shiba_experiment.tsv

The HTML can be copied independently of its export directories. Large outputs and validation previews should remain outside version control.

items.title: Shiba / SnakeShiba configuration
items.text:
Run the complete bulk pipeline with one command:

shiba.py config.yaml -p 8

The pipeline runs transcript assembly, event extraction, junction counting, factorial splicing analysis, expression abundance, PCA, and reporting. Use --mame to stop after splicing, or --start-step 4 to reuse existing events and junction counts under the configured workdir. R/glmmTMB and jsonlite must be available to the configured rscript; see the installation guide.

Set stat_method: beta_binomial to enable factorial regression. Set stat_method: fisher (the default) to select Fisher testing instead. This single setting controls which splicing analysis is run; no additional Boolean switch is needed. Supply workdir, gtf, and experiment_table as usual. The experiment table must contain sample, bam, and group; sample IDs must match the metadata and count columns. A separate sample_metadata file is optional if the experiment table already contains all formula variables. Paths are interpreted relative to the invocation directory; absolute paths are recommended for both Python and Snakemake workflows.

Add these settings to the usual bulk configuration (see the example file):

stat_method: beta_binomial
sample_metadata: /path/to/samples.tsv
formula: genotype * treatment + batch
coef:
  - genotypeKO:treatmentDrug
reference_levels:
  genotype: WT
  treatment: Control
categorical: [batch]
minimum_reads: 10
min_sample_fraction: 0.5
# Optional override; default includes every categorical factor, including batch:
# filter_group: [genotype, treatment]
p_adjust: BH

reference_group and alternative_group are not required for regression. The pipeline disables ttest in regression mode; explicitly combining -t with regression at the psi.py CLI is rejected. Delete the removed beta_binomial key from existing configurations, even when its value is false. To additionally run the existing pairwise gene-expression analysis, set both expression_reference_group and expression_alternative_group. Otherwise expression abundance and PCA are produced without DESeq2 testing. The splicing formula is not applied to expression analysis.

items.title: scShiba usage
items.text:
After installing with Conda, activate the environment and run:

scshiba.py -p 4 config.yaml

For source execution and the SHIBA_HOME used by internal-script examples, see Locating scripts and workflows. The step scripts below are internal tools, not separate commands on PATH.

usage: scshiba.py [-h] [-p PROCESS] [-s START_STEP] [-v] config

scShiba - Pipeline for identification of differential RNA splicing in single-cell RNA-seq data

Step 1: gtf2event.py
    - Converts GTF files to event format.
Step 2: sc2junc.py
    - Counts junction and RI boundary reads from BAM/CRAM files with Tosa.
Step 3: scpsi.py
    - Calculates PSI values and performs differential analysis.
Step 4: plots.py
    - Generates an interactive summary.html report.

positional arguments:
  config                Config file in yaml format

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -p PROCESS, --process PROCESS
                        Number of processors to use (default: 1)
  -s START_STEP, --start-step START_STEP
                        Start the pipeline from the specified step (default: 0, run all steps)
  -v, --verbose         Verbose mode

Please check the Quick start to learn how to prepare the config.yaml.

The above command will run the following steps:

  1. gtf2event.py
  2. sc2junc.py
  3. scpsi.py
  4. plots.py

items.title: Step2: sc2junc.py
items.text:
usage: sc2junc.py [-h] -i INPUT -r RI_EVENT -o OUTPUT -g GTF [-p PROCESSORS] [-a ANCHOR] [-b BOUNDARY_ANCHOR] [-m MIN_INTRON] [-M MAX_INTRON] [-s STRAND] [-v]

Count single-cell junction and RI boundary reads from tagged BAM/CRAM files with Tosa.

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -i INPUT, --input INPUT
                        sample/alignment/barcode experiment table
  -r RI_EVENT, --ri-event RI_EVENT
                        EVENT_RI.txt
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Shiba junctions.bed
  -g GTF, --gtf GTF     GTF used to generate events
  -p PROCESSORS, --processors PROCESSORS
  -a ANCHOR, --anchor ANCHOR
  -b BOUNDARY_ANCHOR, --boundary-anchor BOUNDARY_ANCHOR
                        Bases required on each side of an RI boundary (default: 6)
  -m MIN_INTRON, --min-intron MIN_INTRON
  -M MAX_INTRON, --max-intron MAX_INTRON
  -s STRAND, --strand STRAND
                        XS, RF, FR, or unstranded
  -v, --verbose         Verbose mode

items.title: Step3: scpsi.py
items.text:
usage: scpsi.py [-h] [-p NUM_PROCESS] [-f FDR] [-d PSI] [-r REFERENCE] [-a ALTERNATIVE] [-m MINIMUM_READS] [--onlypsi] [--excel] [-v] junctions event output

PSI calculation for alternative splicing events in scRNA-seq data

positional arguments:
  junctions             A bed file of junction and RI boundary counts generated by sc2junc.py
  event                 Directory that contains text files of alternative splicing events generated by gtf2event.py
  output                Directory for output files

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -p NUM_PROCESS, --num-process NUM_PROCESS
                        Number of processors to use (default: 1)
  -f FDR, --fdr FDR     FDR for detecting differential events (default: 0.05)
  -d PSI, --psi PSI     Threshold of delta PSI for detecting differential events (default: 0.1)
  -r REFERENCE, --reference REFERENCE
                        Reference group for detecting differential events (default: None)
  -a ALTERNATIVE, --alternative ALTERNATIVE
                        Alternative group for detecting differential events (default: None)
  -m MINIMUM_READS, --minimum-reads MINIMUM_READS
                        Minumum value of total reads for each junction for detecting differential events (default: 10)
  --onlypsi             Just calculate PSI for each sample, not perform statistical tests (default: False)
  --excel               Make result files in excel format (default: False)
  -v, --verbose         Verbose output (default: False)

items.title: Interactive summary report
items.text:
The workflow automatically creates plots/summary.html in the work directory. This self-contained HTML uses the same interactive style as Shiba: enlarged text, muted colors, hover labels, zoom/pan, legend toggling, and Arial with browser-default font fallback. It includes the analysis command, differential-event counts, and volcano and PSI scatter plots for all eight event types, including RI. PNG, PDF, and SVG exports are saved alongside the report.

Single-cell PSI values are aggregated by cell group. This report does not add biological replication or change the Fisher tests. Bulk TPM/PSI PCA panels are not included. With only_psi: True, the report instead shows up to 200 rows per event type and explicitly states that no differential testing was performed.

To regenerate the report from existing results:

python "$SHIBA_HOME/src/plots.py" --single-cell -i /path/to/workdir/results -o /path/to/workdir/plots

Add --only-psi for PSI-only results. The command is retrieved from the saved report.json; use -s 'original analysis command' to supply it explicitly.

items.title: Shiba usage
items.text:
After installing with Conda, activate the environment and run:

shiba.py -p 4 config.yaml

For source execution and the SHIBA_HOME used by internal-script examples, see Locating scripts and workflows. The step scripts below are internal tools, not separate commands on PATH.

usage: shiba.py [-h] [-p PROCESS] [-s START_STEP] [--mame] [-v] config

Shiba - Pipeline for identification of differential RNA splicing

Step 1: bam2gtf.py
    - Assembles transcript structures based on mapped reads using StringTie.
Step 2: gtf2event.py
    - Converts GTF files to event format.
Step 3: bam2junc.py
    - Extracts junction reads from BAM files.
Step 4: psi.py
    - Calculates PSI values and performs differential analysis.
Step 5: expression.py
    - Analyzes gene expression.
Step 6: pca.py
    - Performs PCA.
Step 7: plots.py
    - Generates plots from results.

positional arguments:
  config                Config file in yaml format

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -p PROCESS, --process PROCESS
                        Number of processors to use (default: 1)
  -s START_STEP, --start-step START_STEP
                        Start the pipeline from the specified step (default: 0, run all steps)
  --mame                Execute MameShiba, a lightweight version of Shiba, for only splicing analysis. Steps 5-7 will be skipped.
  -v, --verbose         Verbose mode

Check the Quick start to learn how to prepare the config.

The shiba.py command will run the following steps sequentially (transcript assembly is skipped when unannotated: False):

  1. bam2gtf.py
  2. gtf2event.py
  3. bam2junc.py
  4. psi.py
  5. expression.py
  6. pca.py
  7. plots.py

items.title: Step1: bam2gtf.py
items.text:
usage: bam2gtf.py [-h] -i INPUT -r REFERENCE -o OUTPUT [-p PROCESSORS] [-v]

Pipeline for transcript assembly using StringTie

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -i INPUT, --input INPUT
                        Experiment table
  -r REFERENCE, --reference REFERENCE
                        Reference GTF file
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Assembled GTF file
  -p PROCESSORS, --processors PROCESSORS
                        Number of processors to use (default: 1)

items.title: Step3: bam2junc.py
items.text:
usage: bam2junc.py [-h] -i INPUT -r RI_EVENT -o OUTPUT -g GTF [-p PROCESSORS] [-a ANCHOR] [-b BOUNDARY_ANCHOR] [-m MIN_INTRON] [-M MAX_INTRON] [-s STRAND] [-v]

Count junction and RI boundary reads with Tosa and write Shiba's junctions.bed.

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -i INPUT, --input INPUT
                        Experiment table
  -r RI_EVENT, --ri-event RI_EVENT
                        Intron retention event file
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output junction read counts file
  -g GTF, --gtf GTF    GTF used to generate events
  -p PROCESSORS, --processors PROCESSORS
                        Number of processors to use (default: 1)
  -a ANCHOR, --anchor ANCHOR
                        Minimum anchor length (default: 8)
  -b BOUNDARY_ANCHOR, --boundary-anchor BOUNDARY_ANCHOR
                        Bases required on each side of an RI boundary (default: 6)
  -m MIN_INTRON, --min-intron MIN_INTRON
                        Minimum intron size (default: 70)
  -M MAX_INTRON, --max-intron MAX_INTRON
                        Maximum intron size (default: 500000)

Tosa writes gzip-compressed junction and boundary tables for each BAM. Shiba converts their coordinates, combines strand rows, adds zero-count RI boundaries, and writes junctions/junctions.bed. For SnakeShiba, bam2junc.py run processes a single BAM and bam2junc.py merge combines the per-sample tables.

items.title: Step4: psi.py
items.text:
The options below describe the Fisher workflow (stat_method: fisher, the default). For stat_method: beta_binomial, see the factorial quick start and regression CLI and output reference. Run python "$SHIBA_HOME/src/psi.py" --help for the complete current option list.

usage: psi.py [-h] [-p NUM_PROCESS] [-g GROUP] [-f FDR] [-d PSI] [-r REFERENCE] [-a ALTERNATIVE] [-m MINIMUM_READS] [-i] [-t] [--onlypsi] [--onlypsi-group] [--excel] [-v] junctions event output

PSI calculation for alternative splicing events

positional arguments:
  junctions             A bed file of junction read counts generated by bam2junc.py
  event                 Directory that contains text files of alternative splicing events generated by gtf2event.py
  output                Directory for output files

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -p NUM_PROCESS, --num-process NUM_PROCESS
                        Number of processors to use (default: 1)
  -g GROUP, --group GROUP

items.title: SnakeScShiba Usage
items.text:
This snakescshiba.smk script is written for use with Snakemake, a workflow management system that allows for the creation of reproducible and scalable data analyses. Snakemake uses a Python-based domain-specific language to define rules that specify how to generate output files from input files. These rules are executed in a directed acyclic graph (DAG) to ensure efficient and correct execution.

Key Features of Snakemake:

  • Automatically determines the order of execution based on dependencies.
  • Supports parallel execution on local machines, clusters, and cloud environments.
  • Provides built-in support for logging, benchmarking, and resource management.

Tip

For more information about Snakemake, visit:

  • Official Documentation: https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/
  • GitHub Repository: https://github.com/snakemake/snakemake
  • Tutorials and Examples: https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorial/tutorial.html

Set SHIBA_HOME and follow the container setup before running this example. To use the activated Conda environment instead, omit --use-singularity and --singularity-args.

snakemake -s "$SHIBA_HOME/snakescshiba.smk" \
--configfile config.yaml \
--cores 4 \
--use-singularity \
--singularity-args "--bind $HOME:$HOME" \
--rerun-incomplete

Please check the Quick Start to learn how to prepare the config.yaml.

items.title: Workflow
items.text:
Event extraction → per-library Tosa counting → group aggregation → PSI/Fisher analysis → interactive report.

Snakemake schedules independent rules according to their dependencies.

items.title: Interactive summary report
items.text:
The workflow automatically creates plots/summary.html in the work directory. This self-contained HTML uses the same interactive style as Shiba: enlarged text, muted colors, hover labels, zoom/pan, legend toggling, and Arial with browser-default font fallback. It includes the analysis command, differential-event counts, and volcano and PSI scatter plots for all eight event types, including RI. PNG, PDF, and SVG exports are saved alongside the report.

Single-cell PSI values are aggregated by cell group. This report does not add biological replication or change the Fisher tests. Bulk TPM/PSI PCA panels are not included. With only_psi: True, the report instead shows up to 200 rows per event type and explicitly states that no differential testing was performed.

To regenerate the report from existing results, use the SHIBA_HOME set above:

python "$SHIBA_HOME/src/plots.py" --single-cell -i /path/to/workdir/results -o /path/to/workdir/plots

Add --only-psi for PSI-only results. The command is retrieved from the saved report.json; use -s 'original analysis command' to supply it explicitly.
